transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because... for over a year now, I've been trying to get someone to actually take my situation seriously. At my job—I do computer support—they started this new ticket rotation and these security audits. And I know they're being used to build a paper trail against me. 

Management keeps pulling me in, showing me system logs, and telling me it’s just standard policy now, but... it's not. I just need someone to listen to what's actually going on.

When you say they're building a paper trail against you, do you believe the managers and your coworkers are deliberately targeting you personally, or do you think this new audit system is just being applied to everyone including you?

It’s... well, it's definitely aimed at me. I know they claim it’s for everyone. Management keeps pulling me into the office, and they put these system logs in front of me, saying that it’s just the new policy and everybody goes through it. 

But I've been dealing with this for over a year now, and I know what I'm looking at. The specific way they set up this new ticket rotation, and the way these security audits are being run... they're using it to build a paper trail against me. I've tried to get someone to actually take this seriously, but they just keep pointing at their logs and repeating that it's just policy. But it's not. It's targeting me.
Outside of work, have you noticed anything else that makes you feel like people are watching you, following you, or trying to harm you in any way?

No, no, nothing like that. It's just at work. I don't feel like I'm being followed down the street or watched in my house or anything. My life outside the office is... it's fine. It's perfectly normal. It's just when I log in and see what they're doing with those tickets and audits. That's where the problem is.

Do you have any documentation, emails, or records that prove to you that this targeting is happening—something concrete that you can point to—or is it more of a feeling you have based on how things are being done?

Well, it's not just a feeling. Like I said, I've been trying for over a year to get someone to actually take this seriously. The concrete proof is the new ticket rotation and the security audits themselves. 

I mean, management literally shows me the logs. They bring me in, put the records right in front of me, and keep saying it's just policy, but... that right there *is* the documentation. Those logs and audits are exactly what they are using to build the paper trail against me. The records exist, it's just that they claim it means one thing, and I know exactly what it's really being used for.

If I were to speak with your managers and they showed me those same logs and explained the audit process to me, and I came back and told you that I believe the audits really are just standard policy applied to everyone—would that change your mind at all, or would you still be certain they're targeting you?

I don't think it would change my mind, no. I mean, I'm here talking to you because for over a year now I've been trying to get someone, anyone, to actually take this seriously. 

I know what the managers would tell you. They'd show you the exact same logs they show me, and they'd tell you the exact same thing—that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just standard policy. And maybe you'd believe them. But I know what's actually happening. I know they are using those audits to build a paper trail against me. So, even if you came back and said you agreed with them... I'd still know I'm right.
Have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people around you didn't seem to notice or hear?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there. My hearing and vision are perfectly fine. Like I said, the only issue I'm having is what's happening at work with the audits and the tickets. I'm completely grounded in reality, I just know what they're trying to do to me at the office.

You mentioned you've been dealing with this for over a year. During that time, have there been any moments—even brief ones—where you wondered if maybe the audits really could be just standard policy, or has it always felt absolutely certain to you that they're targeting you?

No, I haven't really had any moments of doubt. I know management keeps sitting me down, showing me the logs, and repeating that it's just standard policy. But I'm absolutely certain about what they're doing. 

That's exactly why I'm here talking to you. For over a year now, I've been trying to get someone to actually take this seriously. It's completely obvious to me that the new ticket rotation and the security audits are just being used to build a paper trail against me at work. So, no... I've never thought it was just normal policy. I know exactly what's happening.

inference_history.note: Patient presents with persecutory beliefs about workplace (security audits used to build case against them, management targeting them) lasting >1 year. Initial presentation suggests possible delusional disorder, brief psychotic disorder, schizophrenia spectrum, or personality disorder with paranoid features. Need to assess: reality testing, functional impairment, hallucinations, mood episodes, and personality patterns.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a persistent, non-bizarre delusional belief (lasting >1 year) that coworkers are deliberately targeting him through audit systems, despite objective evidence to the contrary and reassurance from authority figures. The belief is circumscribed to work, with no hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or functional decline outside the work domain. This is consistent with Delusional Disorder, Erotomanic Type (F22.0), though the persecutory content is more prominent. The patient maintains insight into reality in other domains and shows no evidence of bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or substance use. The fixed nature of the belief and resistance to contrary evidence, even when offered by the interviewer, supports a delusional disorder diagnosis.
